eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from the Met Office and global models centers on a daytime maximum of 26°C in London on August 26, 2026, with afternoon peaks near 26–27°C amid easterly to southeasterly flow, increasing cloud, and scattered showers.** 

This positions 26°C as the market favorite at 42.5% implied probability, followed by 25°C (26%) and 27°C (18.5%). Recent observations on August 25 showed clear skies and highs around 24–26°C under moderate easterly winds, setting up a warm but increasingly humid and unsettled pattern for the following day. Thundery showers are expected to develop, especially from mid-morning onward, which could cap peaks or allow brief brighter intervals to push readings slightly higher depending on exact timing and coverage. 

Model agreement is reasonably tight for this short-range outlook, though minor differences in shower placement and boundary-layer moisture explain the spread toward 25°C or 27°C. Historical August norms for London sit near 21–23°C, so current guidance reflects a modestly above-average day tempered by the incoming Atlantic influence. The highest temperature will be recorded at official stations such as Heathrow, with final resolution hinging on the afternoon maximum before any evening cooling.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent showers and thunderstorms expected tomorrow under a moist southwesterly flow are capping the maximum near the historical August average of 31°C, producing the tight market split between 30°C and 31°C.** 

The Hong Kong Observatory’s official outlook for August 26 forecasts a high of 31°C (range 27–31°C) with high rainfall probability and occasional heavy downpours that reduce insolation and promote evaporative cooling. Ensemble guidance shows similar values around 30–31°C, with model spread arising mainly from the timing and intensity of convective cells rather than large-scale temperature advection. Traders therefore assign the highest implied probabilities to the two most likely outcomes while discounting higher values, as sustained cloud cover and rain would suppress peaks below the 32–33°C levels seen on clearer days. Updated HKO guidance or afternoon model runs remain the key near-term catalysts.

Scientific drivers include daytime solar heating under partly cloudy to sunny conditions, moderated by onshore marine influence and light winds that limit extreme warming. The long-term August 26 climatological average high of 75.5°F provides context, while recent regional ridging has supported above-normal readings without pushing into record territory. Minor smoke advection from wildfires may slightly suppress maximums by reducing insolation.

Lower probabilities for 80–81°F (16.5%) account for upside uncertainty if skies clear more than anticipated, while sub-75°F outcomes remain discounted given persistent warmth. Updated NWS briefings and afternoon model guidance on the 25th represent the key near-term catalysts that could refine these implied probabilities ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models indicate London will likely see a daytime maximum of 24–26°C on August 27, 2026, with market-implied odds clustering tightly around 24°C (29%) and 25°C (30%).** This reflects genuine near-term uncertainty in how quickly thundery showers and increased cloud cover will arrive and suppress peak heating.

A transition from relatively settled high pressure earlier in the week to a more unsettled pattern is the dominant driver. Easterly to southeasterly winds are giving way to southerly and southwesterly flow, advecting warmer but moister air from the continent while increasing the likelihood of convective showers and thunderstorms, especially during the afternoon. Official guidance from the Met Office highlights a yellow thunderstorm warning and notes that daytime temperatures will remain near or slightly above seasonal normals (late-August London averages hover near 22–24°C), but heavy cloud and rainfall will limit surface heating.

Key variables differentiating the narrow range of outcomes include the precise timing, coverage, and intensity of showers: prolonged or widespread rain and thick stratiform cloud would favor the lower end (23–24°C) by reducing incoming solar radiation, while any breaks allowing stronger insolation could push readings to 25–26°C. Wind speed and direction also matter—lighter winds under broken cloud permit localized warming, whereas stronger southwesterlies enhance mixing and cooling. Ensemble spread in short-range models remains modest but sufficient to keep the two leading bins nearly even in trader consensus.

Upcoming high-resolution model runs and updated Met Office or ECMWF guidance over the next 24–48 hours will likely tighten the range as the exact evolution of the frontal system and associated convection becomes clearer. Historical analogs for late-August thundery breakdowns in southeast England show similar day-to-day variability in maxima of 2–3°C depending on convective timing.

**Forecasts from major models and agencies place Milan's expected high for August 27 in the 29–32°C range, supporting the market's concentration of probability on 29–31°C outcomes.** Numerical guidance from the ECMWF, GFS, UK Met Office, and BBC Weather shows daytime maxima near 30–31°C under partly to mostly cloudy skies, light easterly or variable winds, and stable high pressure typical of late-summer Po Valley conditions. This aligns with seasonal climatology, where Milan highs decline from mid-August peaks toward the long-term August average of roughly 28–30°C.

Recent model runs have narrowed the spread after earlier warmth (including a mid-August heat episode with red alerts), with consensus favoring modest cooling or stabilization rather than renewed extremes. Key variables include limited moisture return that could cap insolation and any subtle steering changes that might introduce more cloud cover. The tight clustering of implied probabilities around 30°C (37.5%) reflects traders weighting the most consistent ensemble members while assigning lower odds to outliers below 29°C or at/above 32°C, consistent with observed historical variability and the two-day lead time before resolution. Updated model cycles over the next 24–48 hours will likely refine these odds further.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from Chinese meteorological agencies and global models point to a peak maximum temperature of 37–38°C in Chongqing on August 27, shaped by persistent subtropical high pressure that has sustained the regional heatwave, offset by peripheral moisture and scattered showers from Typhoon Zitan. High humidity and light winds typical of the Sichuan Basin limit radiative cooling overnight while increasing afternoon instability, with ensemble guidance showing only modest day-to-day variation. These conditions explain the tight clustering of market-implied odds around 37°C and 38°C, reflecting trader assessment of narrow but genuine uncertainty in the final observed maximum before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model runs show notable spread in Beijing's August 27 maximum temperature forecasts, with official guidance and ensembles centering near 26–29 °C amid light rain or partial clearing after widespread showers on the 25th–26th. Cloud cover, timing of any showers, and northerly flow strength are the key variables separating the closely matched 28 °C and 29 °C outcomes from 27 °C or 30 °C; thicker stratiform clouds or earlier rain suppress insolation and cap highs, while earlier breaks allow stronger afternoon heating. Historical late-August baselines near 29–30 °C provide context, yet the active pattern and short lead time keep resolution sensitive to the next 24–48 hours of observational updates and model consensus shifts.

Cooler surface conditions established earlier in the week, with temperatures running 2–4 °C below average, have reinforced trader positioning around these values. Minor model spread on exact peak timing or localized cloud bands keeps 17 °C and 20 °C as plausible outliers, but consensus data favor the current market-implied distribution centered near 18 °C.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rpll

If NOAA data is unavailable or missing for the observation period, Weather Underground will be used as the secondary resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwest monsoon (habagat) flow and associated cloud cover over western Luzon are the dominant factors keeping Manila’s daytime maxima near seasonal norms of 30–31°C. PAGASA outlooks for August 27 show forecast highs clustered between 29–32°C amid scattered showers and thunderstorms that reduce incoming solar radiation and enhance evaporative cooling. Model consensus indicates limited clearing windows, making 30°C or 31°C the most probable outcomes while suppressing odds of 33°C or higher. Recent monsoon persistence without an approaching tropical cyclone has reinforced trader expectations for modest temperatures rather than extreme heat. Updated PAGASA guidance and high-resolution model runs over the next 48 hours will refine the precise maximum before market resolution.
